The must-sees

13 places Wizzy will tap you for first, each with a story and something to look for.

  1. 01
    Square

    Castle Square

    Like the rest of the Old Town it lay in ruins in 1945 and was rebuilt after the war. It is where the Royal Route to Wilanów begins.

    Look for

    At the square’s southern edge, the white front of St Anne’s Church. Its bell tower has a terrace that looks back over the square and the castle.

  2. 02
    Landmark · 1948

    Monument to the Ghetto Heroes

    Nathan Rapoport’s monument was unveiled in 1948 to honour the Warsaw Ghetto Uprising of 1943. West German Chancellor Willy Brandt knelt before it in 1970.

    Look for

    Walk round to the back: a relief shows Jews being driven to deportation under German helmets and bayonets.

  3. 03
    Square

    Old Town Market Square

    The Old Town was almost entirely destroyed in 1944 and rebuilt using old paintings, photographs and drawings. That reconstruction earned it a place on the UNESCO World Heritage list in 1980.

    Look for

    In the middle of the square stands the bronze Warsaw Mermaid, raising a sword behind her shield. She is the city’s emblem.

  4. 04
    Museum · 2013

    POLIN Museum of the History of Polish Jews

    Designed by the Finnish architects Lahdelma & Mahlamäki, it stands in what was the heart of the ghetto. Its exhibition covers a thousand years of Jewish life in Poland.

    Look for

    Inside, the painted wooden ceiling of the 17th-century Gwoździec synagogue has been reconstructed in full colour, using traditional tools.

  5. 05
    Building · 1955

    Palace of Culture and Science

    Built from 1952 to 1955 as a gift from the Soviet Union, it was designed by Lev Rudnev. It holds theatres, cinemas, museums and a viewing terrace on the 30th floor.

    Look for

    Look along the top of each tier: the stone parapets copy Renaissance attics from Polish towns that Rudnev’s team toured before designing it.

  6. 06
    Palace

    Palace on the Isle

    It began as a 17th-century bathhouse, which gave the park its name. Stanisław August had it rebuilt as his summer residence.

    Look for

    On the bridge to the north stands King John III Sobieski on horseback, trampling a Turkish soldier. Stanisław August raised it in 1788.

  7. 07
    Palace

    Royal Castle

    Home of Polish kings and the parliament, it was blown up by German troops in 1944. It was rebuilt in the 1970s and 1980s, largely paid for by public donations, and is now a museum.

  8. 08
    Park

    Royal Łazienki Park

    King Stanisław August Poniatowski turned it into his summer retreat in the late 18th century. Today it is the city’s favourite place for a long walk.

    Look for

    Find the bronze Chopin seated under a stylised willow by the pond. Summer piano recitals beside him are a long Warsaw tradition.

  9. 09
    Landmark · 1644

    Sigismund’s Column

    Władysław IV raised it in 1644 to honour his father Sigismund III, who moved the capital from Kraków to Warsaw. The column was blown up in 1944, and pieces of its old shafts lie beside the castle.

  10. 10
    Landmark · 1925

    Tomb of the Unknown Soldier

    The arcade is the only fragment left of the Saxon Palace, blown up by the Germans in 1944. The tomb was dedicated in 1925 and the guard changes on the hour.

    Look for

    The plaques on the pillars name battlefields where Polish soldiers fought, from the Middle Ages to modern times.

  11. 11
    Landmark · 1989

    Warsaw Uprising Monument

    Unveiled on 1 August 1989, the 45th anniversary of the Uprising, it stands near a manhole the fighters used to move through the sewers. During communist rule the Uprising could not be openly commemorated.

    Look for

    Behind the monument, the green columns of the Supreme Court are inscribed with Latin legal maxims.

  12. 12
    Museum · 2004

    Warsaw Uprising Museum

    It opened in 2004, 60 years after the 63-day rising against German occupation. The Uprising cost the lives of tens of thousands of fighters and civilians.

    Look for

    Inside, a full-size replica of a B-24 Liberator bomber recalls the Allied crews who flew supply drops to the insurgents.

  13. 13
    Palace

    Wilanów Palace

    It was built for King John III Sobieski, victor at the Siege of Vienna in 1683. In 1805 it became one of the first public museums in Poland.
